findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds a bare gitlink `sentry-repo` at the repository root with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry, which is not a valid submodule registration. Any fresh clone or `git submodule update --init` fails: Git sees an embedded-repo reference with no URL configured, and CI checkouts get an empty/unusable `sentry-repo` directory; CI may also fail on untracked-embedded-repo checks. The file must be removed or properly registered in `.gitmodules`.

[BUG] `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count()`, whose SnQL aggregate sums a `sample_weight` column that nothing in the repository writes or defines. The only place `sample_rate` is derived is `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` in factories (a test helper setting a promoted tag, not a `sample_weight` column). No ingest path, migration, or snuba schema change in this diff creates `sample_weight`, so the generated SnQL `sum(Column("sample_weight"))` fails at query resolution with an unknown-column error for real traffic, and the new test `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects` (tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py, asserting `count == 10`) fails because no writer produces the weight of 10 it expects.

[BUG] The `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is registered only in the discover dataset's `function_converter`, but `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset (src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:119-121), so errors-dataset queries receive the `upsampled_count()` column. An errors-dataset stats request with all projects allowlisted emits a query containing `upsampled_count()` that the errors dataset's function registry does not define, producing a query-resolution failure (400/500) instead of an upsampled count — the exact path the feature is meant to serve. The function must also be registered in the errors dataset (or the errors path must not apply the transform).

[ADVISORY] The eligibility cache writes results into the shared default cache under an org+project-ids key, keyed by `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`, while tests patch `options` per-test. The four endpoint tests in tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py share the same org/project IDs and run against the real cache: an earlier test caches `is_eligible` (e.g. True in the allowlisted test), and a later test with a mocked empty allowlist reads the stale cached True and applies upsampling, so `test_error_upsampling_with_no_allowlisted_projects` and `test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist` fail non-deterministically depending on test order/parallelism. Also, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has no caller anywhere in the diff, so production allowlist changes propagate only after the 60s TTL.

[ADVISORY] `_is_error_focused_query` performs a raw substring check for `"event.type:error"` in the lowercased query string, which matches false positives such as `event.type:error_unique` or a quoted/negated value like `-event.type:error`. A discover query with `!event.type:error` (errors excluded) or any token containing the substring flips the branch to apply `upsampled_count()` on a query whose rows are not all errors, mixing sample weights over non-error events. This is a present trigger reachable via the public `query` parameter, not hypothetical.

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is a public function with zero call sites in this diff and its key construction cannot match writes for arbitrary project subsets anyway. Operators changing `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` have no path to invalidate the cache, so eligibility lags by the full 60s TTL with no documented/automated hook; the function also only deletes the exact sorted-project-id combination passed, so any different project combination cached during that window stays stale — a ships-inert invalidation API.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query uses a raw substring match on 'event.type:error' in the query string, so negated or unrelated queries are misclassified as error-focused. A discover-dataset query like `query=!event.type:error` (or any string merely containing 'event.type:error' as a substring) returns True, so count() is silently replaced with sum(sample_weight) on a query that excludes error events — users on allowlisted projects get inflated/wrong counts with no error, since transaction events lack sample_weight.

[BUG] test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist asserts un-upsampled counts but shares the module-level cache key with test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects, which cached is_eligible=True for the same (org, project_ids) pair for 60 seconds. When the tests run against a shared/persistent cache (memcached/redis in CI), the second test hits the cached True, applies the upsampled count, and asserts count==1 against an actual value of 10 — a test-ordering failure that makes the allowlist check appear broken when it is the cache that is unvalidated; no test in the diff covers the 60s cache at all.

[ADVISORY] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only matches the exact string 'count()' (lowercased/stripped), leaving aliased counts and derived aggregations untransformed. Dashboard/widget queries using 'count() as total', equations like 'count_unique(user)', or any yAxis with an alias bypass upsampling silently — for allowlisted projects the same chart shows upsampled counts for one yAxis spelling and raw counts for another, and no test in the diff covers an aliased count() despite this being the dominant real-world shape sent by dashboards.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff, and no code path updates the allowlist option with invalidation, so the documented invalidation hook is dead code. Operators who change 'issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist' get up to 60 seconds of stale eligibility per (org, project-set) key with no way to force invalidation; the function exists to satisfy the design but nothing invokes it, and no test exercises it.

[ADVISORY] The diff fabricates sample_rate only inside the test factory (_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling in store_event), with no production ingest/normalization path writing sample_weight for allowlisted projects anywhere in this diff. The endpoint tests pass because the factory injects client_sample_rate into normalized_data, but real events ingested outside tests never gain sample_rate/sample_weight on this code path — if the referenced schema/pipeline doesn't populate it, sum(sample_weight) yields 0 or NULL in production while every test in the diff is green; the real pipeline is asserted nowhere in this diff (the sentry-repo submodule pointer is the only hint it exists elsewhere).

[ADVISORY] The 60-second eligibility cache is keyed on (org, sorted project_ids) but not on the dataset or query, and the cached boolean is trusted across all request contexts that share those projects. Any mid-request change to the allowlist option yields inconsistent results between the cached eligibility check and the actual query execution within a single dashboard refresh, and mixed-dataset dashboards hitting the same project set share one cache entry — the consistency window is documented only in a docstring, with no acceptance criterion or test defining the intended staleness behavior for allowlist removal (a project removed from the allowlist keeps showing 10x counts for up to 60s with no verification of that bound).

[BUG] The diff adds a new gitlink for a submodule 'sentry-repo' at commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a that is completely untraceable to the stated intent of error-count upsampling. An unexplained submodule pointer enters the repo: CI checkouts and deployments pull in unknown code at an arbitrary commit, with no review of its contents and no relation to the PR's stated requirement.

[BUG] The diff introduces a `sample_weight`-based aggregation (`sum(sample_weight)` via `upsampled_count()`) but nothing anywhere in the diff writes a `sample_weight` value — the only data-side change sets `sample_rate` in the test factory, which no code in this diff maps to a `sample_weight` column. For real requests against allowlisted projects, `sum(sample_weight)` reads a column that is never populated by the event pipeline, so counts silently return 0/null instead of upsampled counts; the invariant the PR claims (upsampled error counts) is not enforced anywhere end-to-end.

[BUG] `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` caches the eligibility result in the shared `cache` backend keyed on org+projects for 60s, but no caller in the diff ever calls the provided `invalidate_upsampling_cache`, and the cache is also unversioned against option changes. When an operator removes a project from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, queries keep using `upsampled_count()` (sum over a possibly-missing sample_weight) for up to 60s after the config change, returning wrong counts with no code path in this diff able to correct it.

[ADVISORY] The diff silently rewrites the topEvents validation message from "If topEvents needs to be at least 1" to "topEvents needs to be at least 1", unrelated to the upsampling feature. Unrelated behavior-visible change smuggled into a feature PR; API clients matching on the error string (or contract tests pinning it) break without any requirement tracing to this diff.

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined and exported but has zero call sites anywhere in the diff — no signal handler, options-change hook, or admin path invokes it. The documented cache-consistency mechanism is inert code; the next maintainer assumes allowlist changes invalidate the cache when they do not, and the function will drift from the actual cache key format.

[ADVISORY] The docstring of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` states "reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time ... intentional to ensure we always have the latest configuration state", which directly contradicts the caller's 60-second cache the same module implements. A future maintainer reading the helper believes eligibility checks are always fresh and will build on that assumption; the comment encodes a guarantee the module itself violates within the same file.

[ADVISORY] `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` uses two blanket `except Exception: pass` blocks and mutates the shared `store_event` factory for all tests in the codebase, a scope expansion beyond the stated PR intent (an API stats feature). Every test storing any event now silently gains a `sample_rate` whenever contexts contain error_sampling data, and swallowed exceptions hide malformed context shapes; unrelated tests can start failing or passing for reasons they cannot trace to this diff.

[ADVISORY] The diff gates upsampling only inside the stats endpoint's query execution, applying the transformation identically at three hand-repeated sites (`if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)`) rather than once where `query_columns` is derived. The next endpoint that reuses the eligibility check (issue list counts, tag stats) must re-implement the same gating; any of the three duplicated sites being missed during refactor yields silently non-upsampled counts for one query path.

[BUG] The eligibility cache key is built with Python's builtin hash() over a tuple of project ids, and the cached boolean is read with `cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(...)` while the cache-miss path stores only the allowlist result — but the real defect is that the cache is never invalidated: invalidate_upsampling_cache has zero call sites anywhere in the diff. When an operator removes a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist, every org-events-stats response for that org keeps applying sum(sample_weight) upsampling for up to 60 seconds (and longer under a persistent cache), returning inflated counts to existing dashboards/alerts after the feature has been disabled; the invalidate function is dead code.

[BUG] The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction aggregates Column("sample_weight"), but nothing in this diff writes a sample_weight column to Snuba for error events — the only related producer is the test factory's _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling which sets `sample_rate` on normalized event data, not `sample_weight`, and there is no mapping from one to the other anywhere in the diff. For allowlisted projects every count() on the org-events-stats endpoint becomes toInt64(sum(sample_weight)), which is 0/NULL for events whose ingestion path never sets sample_weight — dashboards that previously showed real counts now show 0 (or drop rows), and the endpoint's tests asserting count==10 will fail because no code computes sample_weight = 1/client_sample_rate.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query does a raw substring test `"event.type:error" in query` on the lowercased query string, so it returns True for any query merely containing that substring, including negated (`!event.type:error` or `-event.type:error`) and partially-matching values. A discover-dataset query for `!event.type:error` (all transaction/non-error events) is classified as error-focused and count() is rewritten to sum(sample_weight) over events that have no sample_weight, returning 0 counts on a query that used to return correct non-error counts; the substring match cannot distinguish the polarity or token boundary of the search term.

[ADVISORY] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites the exact string `count()`; every other aggregation in the same yAxes list (count_unique(...), failure_rate(), percentiles, equations) passes through unchanged, so a mixed-axis chart gets one upsampled axis alongside raw axes computed over the same client-side-sampled events. Dashboard widgets with yAxis=count(),count_unique(user) on an allowlisted org will show an upsampled event count next to an unupsampled unique-user count, producing internally inconsistent charts (e.g. 10,000 events from 3 users) that undermine trust in the feature the moment users combine columns.

[ADVISORY] The upsampling decision `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is consulted only inside `_get_event_stats`, but the endpoint has other consumers of the same query/columns elsewhere in the request (e.g. the top-events outer/selected-columns paths and any totals computed by the dataset) that keep using raw count(), so a single response can carry both upsampled and non-upsampled numbers depending on which internal query produced them. Users comparing the timeseries values against the top-events row totals or any other aggregate computed in the same request for the same allowlisted org see mismatched counts, and the check itself performs a cache round-trip plus an options lookup on the hot stats path per request, duplicating the eligibility decision logic that will drift when a second endpoint (issues stats, dashboards previews) adopts upsampling.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a git submodule named `sentry-repo` pointing at commit a5d29095 inside the sentry repository itself, which is almost certainly an accidental `git submodule add` of the repo's own URL and not part of the feature. Every clone/checkout of this branch recursively materializes a nested copy of the entire sentry repo pinned to an arbitrary commit; CI and developers get a stale duplicate tree, and any reviewer trusting that the upsampling Snuba-side changes live in the submodule finds an empty/divergent commit instead — the actual sample_weight producer this PR implies is nowhere.

[BUG] The cache key uses Python's built-in hash() on a tuple of project ids, which is randomized per process under PYTHONHASHSEED, so each web/worker process computes a different key for the same organization+project set. Cache entries are never shared across processes: with N uwsgi/celery processes, the hit rate collapses to per-process only, the claimed 60-second dedup of option lookups does not materialize in any multi-process deployment, and invalidation calls from one process delete a key no other process will ever read.

[BUG] invalidate_upsampling_cache() is defined but has zero call sites anywhere in this diff — no signal handler, option-change hook, or admin path invokes it. When an operator removes a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist, cached eligibility keeps serving upsampled counts for up to 60 seconds, silently returning 10x-inflated error counts to dashboards during the window; the invalidation function is dead code that gives a false impression that this is handled.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query uses a raw substring test ("event.type:error" in query) on the lowercased query string, so it both over- and under-matches: 'event.type:errorX' or any field value containing the literal substring matches, while a discover query selecting errors via '!event.type:transaction' or a bare issue-stream default query matches nothing. Users querying Discover with '!event.type:transaction' get un-upscaled (undercounted) error counts for allowlisted projects, while a query like 'message:"event.type:errormessage"' gets upscaled counts applied to events that have no sample_weight — silent numeric corruption on the happy path the option is supposed to gate.

[BUG] The diff adds a gitlink 'sentry-repo' (new file mode 160000) pointing at commit a5d290951de — an accidental nested repo/submodule marker committed alongside the feature. Anyone cloning the PR gets a broken submodule reference to a path that is not a declared submodule, breaking checkout and CI reproducibility for every consumer of this branch; nothing in the PR description sanctions adding a submodule.

[ADVISORY] The diff silently changes the user-facing 400 message from "If topEvents needs to be at least 1" to "topEvents needs to be at least 1" — an unrelated cosmetic edit smuggled into a PR about error upsampling. This is objective drift accepted by no reviewer sign-off on that specific change; any client (or test) matching the old message string breaks, and it establishes the pattern of unrelated edits riding along in this endpoint.

[ADVISORY] The upsampling decision is computed once, stored in the redundant intermediate variable upsampling_enabled = should_upsample, and then the identical transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns) call is copy-pasted into three separate branches (top_events RPC, top_events legacy, timeseries RPC, timeseries legacy — four sites). The next contributor adding a query path (or fixing one) must remember to re-add the transform at each site; one missed site silently yields non-upsampled counts for the same request shape — the failure is invisible until users compare dashboards. Computing final_columns once at the decision point deletes three conditional blocks and the dead reassignment.

[ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling is now applied unconditionally to every store_event() call in the entire test suite, mutating normalized_data['sample_rate'] whenever a contexts.error_sampling block exists. Any existing or future test that stores an event with an error_sampling context (or where production normalization behavior is being asserted) now silently gets a sample_rate injected by test tooling rather than by the code under test, masking gaps between test fixtures and real event-manager behavior and drifting tests away from production semantics.

[ADVISORY] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites the exact token 'count()' (after lower/strip), leaving 'count() as foo', 'count_unique(...)', and any aliased count untouched, while the intent is 'upsampled error count'. A user issuing yAxis='count() as total' on an allowlisted project gets a raw count next to upsampled counts elsewhere in the same dashboard — mixed-magnitude series that look consistent but are off by the sampling factor, with no error or log indicating partial transformation.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query makes its transform decision with a raw substring match ("event.type:error" in query) on the user-supplied query string, so any query containing that text anywhere triggers the sample_weight aggregation even when the query is not actually filtering to error events. A user querying the discover dataset with e.g. query='!event.type:error' or 'event.type:transaction event.type:error' (or free text containing the literal 'event.type:error') gets the transformed sum(sample_weight) aggregation applied to transaction rows, where sample_weight does not exist — returning wrong/zero counts or a Snuba column error instead of the real data.

[ADVISORY] The 60-second cache of allowlist eligibility means the transform decision is made from a cached value that can disagree with the live option, and invalidate_upsampling_cache is only effective for one exact project-id set with no callers in this diff. When an operator removes a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist, users of that project keep receiving upsampled (inflated) counts for up to 60 seconds after the change; and because the cache key hashes the exact sorted project-id tuple, no in-diff code path ever invalidates it, so the toggle behaves as best-effort rather than authoritative.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a gitlink for a 'sentry-repo' submodule at the repository root pointing to an unrelated commit, with no other reference to it anywhere in the change. Anyone cloning with --recursive fetches and materializes an unreviewed external repository's pinned commit into the tree; if that commit (or a later forced-update of it) contains build hooks or code that gets imported, it is a supply-chain injection vector that ships silently with this PR.

[ADVISORY] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites only the exact form count() into 'upsampled_count() as count' and passes all other user-controlled yAxis columns through untouched, while the alias of the injected function is fixed at 'count' regardless of the original column's alias. A user requesting yAxis 'count_unique(user) as mycount' or 'count()' alongside other aliases gets mixed semantics: the count is silently inflated by sample_weight while every other aggregation (and any pre-aggregation in the same chart) stays unweighted, producing internally inconsistent dashboard numbers that look authoritative.

[ADVISORY] The cache-hit branch of is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects (the actual production entry point) is never exercised by any test — tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py tests only the private helpers and the endpoint tests hit it incidentally. A regression in cache serialization, the `cached_result and _should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)` short-circuit, or a wrong cache key goes unnoticed; the endpoint tests can pass with an always-miss or always-hit cache because none of them asserts which path was taken.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint tests run with the real (locmem) cache and never clear or call invalidate_upsampling_cache between test methods, so eligibility results written by one test method can be read by the next when org/project ids repeat. test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist can read a cached `True` written by test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects when database id sequences repeat across rolled-back test transactions, flipping its `count == 1` assertion to a spurious failure (or masking a real regression with a stale hit).

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query uses a substring match on "event.type:error", so a discover query negating the filter (`-event.type:error` or `event.type:!error`) is classified as error-focused and count() is silently replaced with sum(sample_weight). A user querying discover with a negated error filter (or any token containing the substring, e.g. a saved search with `-event.type:error`) gets upsampled counts instead of raw counts while the response still aliases them as `count` — no test in test_error_upsampling.py covers a negated query because the test table mirrors exactly the cases the implementation already handles.

[ADVISORY] The top_events branch of _get_event_stats (upsampling_enabled -> transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling applied to y_axes/timeseries_columns when top_events > 0) is exercised by zero tests — all four new endpoint tests omit the topEvents parameter. A regression in the top-events upsampling path (e.g. dropping final_columns into only one of the use_rpc/non-RPC call sites, or an alias mismatch breaking the response shape for topEvents widgets) ships undetected; DashboardWidget topEvents consumers get wrong or erroring counts.

[ADVISORY] The end-to-end assertion `count == 10` depends on sample_rate being injected by a test-factory hook (_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling), which only fires in store_event; no production code in this diff writes sample_weight, so the tests verify a test-only pipeline. The endpoint tests pass while production events never receive sample_weight from any writer in the diff (no ingestion/storage change, no option-driven path outside tests); in production sum(sample_weight) over unallowlisted-schema events yields null/0 counts that these tests cannot represent — the upsampled count of 10 is a factory artifact, not evidence the feature works end-to-end.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no callers anywhere in the diff and no test, so the documented cache-consistency mechanism is dead code. Allowlist option changes leave stale eligibility results for up to 60 seconds with no way to force invalidation in practice, and the docstring claim that invalidation 'should be called when the allowlist configuration changes' is never exercised — a refactor breaking the cache-key format in either function goes unnoticed.

[BUG] The count() → sum(sample_weight) transformation is enabled purely by flipping the issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist option, with no backfill guaranteeing that historical events in allowlisted projects actually have a sample_weight value. The code comment says "We rely on the database schema to ensure sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects," but no migration, backfill, or ingestion-path change in this diff creates sample_weight for events already stored before the sampling rollout. The moment an operator adds a project to the allowlist, every previously-ingested event contributes NULL/0 to sum(sample_weight), so dashboards silently report counts of 0 (or gross undercounts) for all pre-rollout data — silent data misrepresentation with no error and no way to detect it from the API response.

[BUG] The only code anywhere in this diff that derives sample_rate from the error_sampling context lives in the test factory (store_event), so the production ingestion pipeline never populates the field the upsampled_count() aggregation depends on. _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling is added to sentry/testutils/factories.py, which runs only under test; the real event-ingestion path (event_manager/normalization) is untouched. In production, events arriving with contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate never get a sample_rate/sample_weight, so the new upsampled_count() SnQL function sums a column nothing writes — a ships-inert data path that makes every upsampled count wrong (likely 0) the instant the allowlist option is enabled in a real deployment. The tests pass only because the factory fakes the exact behavior the production code was supposed to implement.

[BUG] The eligibility decision is cached for 60 seconds keyed only on (organization.id, project_ids), but the dataset/query-shape half of the decision is recomputed fresh, so the cached allowlist result is reused across requests where it may be stale after an operator removes a project from the allowlist. An operator removing a project from issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist to stop upsampling (e.g., because sample_weight data is bad) keeps getting upsampled, potentially zero-valued counts for up to 60 seconds per project-set — during incident response this is exactly when wrong counts hurt. No call site in this diff invokes invalidate_upsampling_cache when the option changes, so the provided invalidation hook is dead code and the 60s TTL is the only consistency mechanism.

[BUG] The upsampled_count SnQL function is registered only in discover.py's function_converter, but _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset, whose query-resolution path may not know this function. When the errors dataset (sentry.snuba.errors) executes the rewritten y_axes containing 'upsampled_count() as count', the function must resolve through the errors dataset's resolver; if that converter (separate from discover's) lacks the registration, the query fails with an unknown-function error and the org-events-stats endpoint 500s for all allowlisted projects on the errors dataset — a cutover with no feature flag to disable except editing the allowlist option under 60s of cache lag.

[BUG] Only the literal string 'count()' is rewritten, so compound/derived aggregations containing count() as a subexpression (equations like 'if(count()>10,...)', 'percent(count(),...)') bypass the upsampling transform while plain count() is upsampled, mixing sampled and unsampled semantics in the same response. A dashboard widget combining yAxis count() with an equation referencing count() gets an upsampled count() series next to an equation computed from raw unsampled count(), producing internally inconsistent data (e.g., percentage of total > 100%) for allowlisted projects; nothing validates that all aggregations in the request were transformed together.

[BUG] upsampled_count() computes toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no handling for NULL/missing sample_weight, so events ingested before the upsampling schema backfill (or from misconfigured clients) are silently dropped from the count while the API returns HTTP 200 success. A user querying a allowlisted project's error count over a window that includes pre-rollout events gets a count that reflects only the events carrying a non-null sample_weight — the historical portion silently vanishes (sum over NULL rows yields NULL/0), reported as a successful, correct-looking stat. No log, no error, no indication the number is partial.

[ADVISORY] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites columns whose lowercased/trimmed text is exactly 'count()', so derived/composite aggregations that internally rely on count() — equations (yAxis 'equation|count()/count_unique(user)'), failure_rate(), and any alias-wrapped count — pass through unchanged in the same response where a plain count() axis is upsampled. Dashboard widgets or stats requests mixing a raw count() axis with an equation or failure_rate axis get inconsistent semantics in one 200 response: one series upsampled, the other raw, with no error surfaced — users comparing the two numbers see them contradict each other.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in this diff (no option-change hook, signal handler, or admin path invokes it), so it is dead code and allowlist changes actually propagate only via the 60-second TTL expiry, not via invalidation. Operators flipping the 'issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist' option believe invalidation is wired up (the function's docstring promises cache consistency 'when the allowlist configuration changes'), but for up to 60 seconds queries against newly-allowlisted or de-allowlisted projects return count numbers computed under the stale eligibility decision — silently wrong totals right at the moment an operator is verifying their config change took effect.

[ADVISORY] The eligibility decision is cached per (organization, hash of project_ids) but the dataset/request half of the predicate (_should_apply_sample_weight_transform) is evaluated uncached after the cache lookup, so the cached value is reused across requests that differ in dataset while the fresh path recomputes the full allowlist check each time — and a Python hash() collision between two distinct project-id tuples returns another org+project-set's cached eligibility. Two different project-id sets whose sorted tuples hash-collide share a cache entry, so one set's eligibility verdict is served for the other's query; the practical trigger is rare but the failure mode is silent wrong-count (a non-allowlisted project set gets upsampled counts, or vice versa) with no error anywhere. Also, every 60-second miss writes to the shared cache on the request hot path, adding one cache write per org+project-set per minute of traffic.

goldens.comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

Two different project-id sets whose sorted tuples hash-collide share a cache entry, so one set's eligibility verdict is served for the other's query; the practical trigger is rare but the failure mode is silent wrong-count (a non-allowlisted project set gets upsampled counts, or vice versa) with no error anywhere. Because `hash()` is not collision-free, two distinct project-id sets within the same organization can theoretically map to the same cache key and thus share an eligibility value, causing silent wrong behavior (upsampling applied or not applied incorrectly). However, the finding’s claim that the cached allowlist decision is incorrectly reused across differing datasets is not accurate here, since `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform(dataset, request)` is evaluated on every path (both cache hit and miss) and is not itself cached.
